continuity.history: .execution/box-v4/ is frozen history for B0-B1.1, D1.1 and D1.2. New work is recorded in waves/<id>.md, STATUS.md and Git.
continuity.sequence: Milestone BT, the bounty tool: BT1 to BT3 are merged. Remaining, each only when named: BT3a (report, do not judge), BT3b (fewer things to supply), BT4 (tell the agent; accepted by constructed scenarios), BT5 (the kitchen uses it: journey, judgement, open observation), BT6 (first bounty outside; owner approval). The research lab is paused. See PLAN.md.

sharedIntegrationPolicy: Each wave brief names its write paths. One writer per branch; the reviewer checks the diff stays inside them. Globs below are planning scope.
evidenceDirectoryPattern: waves/<taskId>.md holds the brief and the reviewer result; verify logs are local under .kitchen/runs/.

tasks.title: Select the supported delegation case and reconcile reusable foundations
deliverables: Record actual W002 acceptance/ownership and the exact reusable Box, auth, Git, environment and evaluation interfaces; distinguish checked source from accepted behavior.

Specify one modular TypeScript fixture repository and two bounded work requests, including a shared dependency, unrelated excluded owner modules, literal completion examples and an unsupported coupling case.

Define the initial buyer/job, documented competitive overlap and an ordinary issue-plus-contributor comparison before final results. Predeclare comparable obligations, input/tool/familiarity differences, observations and classification; do not start a customer study or procure vendor access.
Prepare the first implementation brief with exact integration paths and resource/recipient policy; retain B history and the current implementation candidate.
acceptance: A reviewer can identify the first supported task, required package inputs, owner integration obligations and why no full owner clone should be necessary.

The comparison protocol accounts for common onboarding, per-task preparation, recipient setup, owner verification/integration and rework; missing observations and commercial evidence remain unverified.
No current lease is taken or old task accepted by inference. Dependent implementation awaits independently accepted B1.1 or an explicit separately approved replacement foundation.
verification: Independent source/interface and fixture-design review; read-only reconciliation, no product test or new resource is required for this planning unit.

tasks.title: Verify on the host without Docker
deliverables: Refresh the lockfile so packages/box-contracts is installed by a normal frozen install; today test:box-contracts cannot resolve zod on the host.
Add an embedded Postgres provider to scripts/verify.mjs and make it the default, so verification needs no Docker.
Box test helpers accept the disposable database verify provides: no fixed container hostname, no database cap, each run creates and drops its own databases.
Remove the W002 verification profile switches from scripts/suite.mjs and scripts/vitest.config.mjs once nothing uses them. Leave scripts/box-verification in place, unused, until a later cleanup.
acceptance: With Docker Desktop stopped, node scripts/verify.mjs test:box-contracts test:box-auth exits 0 on a clean clone after a frozen install.
A second run immediately afterwards also passes and leaves no databases, processes or containers behind.
No assertion in an existing Box test is weakened.
verification: Reviewer repeats both runs with Docker stopped and compares the Box test assertions with master.

tasks.title: Prepare a versioned Box from a work request and completion agreement
reuse: B2.1/B2.2/B4 design seams, not their unverified completion
deliverables: Instantiate the D1.1 fixture design with a pinned isolated owner Git baseline and reproducible fixture registration; shared helpers and excluded modules must be actual source, not prose placeholders.
Direct request or pasted issue body plus registered repository/base produces a draft with grounded facts, observable examples, exclusions and unresolved preparation gaps.
Owner can understand and approve the exact completion agreement through a concise card or input/output example; no mandatory chat, external tracker connector or handwritten technical spec.
Changed agreement creates a new version and invalidates affected approval; intake remains separate from assignment, execution and bounty publication.
acceptance: Both supported requests produce inspectable drafts through the same preparation path. A recorded URL is not claimed as fetched content.
Unresolved consequential requirements and stale approval block readiness. Demo output, live-model evidence and independently assessed requirement quality are distinct.
A request may contain connected full-stack work; the system does not equate each sentence with a separate Box.
verification: Real owner UI/API create, approve and amend flow; independent literal agreement/version/role tests and an omitted-obligation negative case.
tasks.resumption: Held by the CEO on 5 October 2026 as unaccepted work on branch wave/D1.2. Resume after K1: rebase onto master, move its tests to the disposable database, drop its container harness, then review and verify under KITCHEN.md.

tasks.title: Export and validate the actual portable work package
reuse: packages/analyzer import scanning where it fits
deliverables: A Box is a plain folder: box.json (outcome, base commit, read context, editable paths, checks, submission contract), the selected source, the lockfile and tool versions, and non-sensitive fixtures. No server, database or container is required to create or open one.

A command-line export builds that folder from an owner-reviewed manifest and reports every import that leaves the selection, so a missing dependency is a named preparation gap rather than a silent full-repository fallback.
Export validates itself by execution: install and run the declared baseline checks in a clean directory that contains only the package. Excluded modules may be replaced by declared type-only stubs.
Record package inventory, the share of owner source disclosed, transfer sizes and actual preparation effort and corrections.
The agreement can come from a file. The D1.2 store is one source of agreements, not a prerequisite.
acceptance: In a clean directory with no owner repository or history, the package installs, builds its baseline and runs its declared checks using only Node, pnpm and Git.
An omitted dependency, an escaping path or link, an unlisted input and an attempt to reach owner-only source are each rejected with a reason.
Unrelated owner modules are demonstrably absent from the package. Exporting the full owner source cannot pass this gate.
verification: Reviewer runs export and the clean-directory checks on the supported fixture and on one slice of this repository, plus the missing-dependency and boundary negatives.
tasks.approach: Start with a prototype wave: two or three small throwaway attempts at selecting source for one fixture change (for example an owner-written manifest checked by import closure, selection derived from the TypeScript program starting at the editable paths, and type-only stubs for everything outside the editable paths). Compare them on the same clean-directory checks, disclosed-source share and preparation effort, then write the real brief from the winner.

tasks.title: Open the package and submit an exact scoped contribution
reuse: Box attempt identity fields from packages/box-contracts
deliverables: A recipient opens the folder in any editor or hands it to any agent, implements inside the editable paths and runs the local checks.
A command-line submit produces a patch bound to the Box identity, version and base commit, with paths mapped back to owner source.
Record who or what the recipient was, what it was given, setup and investigation effort, and every clarification it needed. For agent recipients also record tokens and whether it succeeded.
The first real recipients are this kitchen's own workers: a wave brief is delivered as a Box.
acceptance: An actual recipient completes open, edit, local check and submit using the package only. A simulated recipient does not count.
Edits outside the editable paths, a wrong Box or base, and an altered agreement are rejected at submit and again at owner verification.
Human and agent recipients use the same package and the same checks.
verification: Reviewer performs a real package-only attempt and the wrong-scope, wrong-version and altered-agreement cases.

tasks.title: Verify the contribution in the original repository and integrate it
reuse: packages/evaluation patch validation where it fits
deliverables: A command-line verify applies the exact submitted patch to a clean checkout of the owner repository at the Box base and runs the owner-side checks, including the surrounding interfaces the package did not contain.
A stale base or failed check blocks integration. On pass, the owner merges through ordinary Git with the Box and attempt identity in the commit message.
Each failure is classified: preparation defect (the package lacked something), environment failure, or implementation failure against a published obligation.
acceptance: A correct supported contribution integrates into real owner Git history with recoverable Box/attempt/review provenance.
Local-pass/full-owner-fail, self-review, stale result and absent merge authority cannot become accepted.
No production release, remote publication or payment is inferred from accepted synthetic integration.
verification: Reviewer runs a real patch through verify and merge on the fixture, plus stale-base, repeat-submission and local-pass-owner-fail negatives.

tasks.title: Move the legacy live tests onto the disposable database
deliverables: The tests named *-live.test.ts that only need a database run against the Postgres that scripts/verify.mjs provides, instead of shelling into the private-task-mvp-synthetic containers.
Tests that genuinely need the running legacy services are listed with the reason and moved out of check into their own package script, unchanged.
check passes twice in a row with no wait, because nothing in it hits the legacy login rate limiter any more.
acceptance: node scripts/verify.mjs exits 0 twice back to back.
No assertion in any moved test is weakened; each still fails when the behaviour it guards is broken.
With the four private-task-mvp-synthetic containers stopped, check still passes.
verification: Reviewer stops the synthetic containers, runs verify twice, restarts them, and compares each ported assertion with master.

tasks.title: Remove the old container verification harness
deliverables: scripts/box-verification/, tests/box/verification/ and the mailbox transport in scripts/docker.mjs are deleted, with the BOX_VERIFICATION_* switches in scripts/suite.mjs and scripts/vitest.config.mjs.
tests/box/auth/fixture-transport.test.ts goes with the transport it tested. This removal of tests is the stated purpose of the wave and is named in its brief.
acceptance: No file references BOX_VERIFICATION_ or scripts/box-verification.
node scripts/verify.mjs test:box-contracts test:box-auth test:box-delegation exits 0.
verification: Reviewer greps for leftovers and confirms no test outside the old harness was removed or changed.

tasks.title: Kitchen numbers page and a stall guard in verify
deliverables: node scripts/kitchen-stats.mjs prints one page from .kitchen/runs and Git: verify minutes per step, runs and failed runs per wave branch, wave duration from first commit to merge, and the three largest costs. No new files to maintain; it only reads.

scripts/verify.mjs counts consecutive non-PASS runs and elapsed time on the current branch from its own run history, and prints a plain STALL line telling the agent to park the wave once a threshold is passed (defaults: 6 consecutive non-PASS committed runs or 90 minutes; thresholds are flags). It never changes the verdict or exit code.

The page also checks the kitchen's own limits and fails loudly when one is broken: AGENTS.md plus KITCHEN.md over 20 KB, kitchen/INBOX.md over ten lines, STATUS.md over one screen (60 lines). It shows usage per wave where wave files record it.
acceptance: On the 5 October night-run logs the page reproduces the known figures: about 120 verify minutes, check about 45.
A test feeds verify a fabricated run history and sees the STALL line appear at the threshold and not before.
PASS, FAIL and UNCOMMITTED verdicts and exit codes are unchanged.
verification: Reviewer recomputes two figures by hand from the summaries and runs the stall test with thresholds on both sides.

tasks.title: Verify speed 1: stop repeating work
deliverables: A step that already passed on this exact commit, with a clean tree, is not run again: verify reads its own summaries, reports the step as reused with the run it came from, and --fresh forces a real run. A reused result is never offered for a dirty tree or a different commit.
A suite named in the brief is not run a second time inside the same invocation when check already ran it.

check runs the typecheck, the boundary check and only the suites whose paths the branch touched since master; a change to shared tooling (scripts/, package.json, the lockfile, test config) runs everything. --full runs every suite, and the head chef runs --full before a milestone closes and before each overnight stop.

KITCHEN.md and the reviewer role say what this means for the pass: it may rely on a recorded PASS for the same commit and spend its time on the diff, the lenses and its own attacks; it runs --fresh when it has any reason to doubt the record.
acceptance: Before and after come from scripts/kitchen-stats.mjs (K4), at least five runs each on the same commit, with spread. Keep a change only if the numbers support it.
A deliberately broken test in a suite the branch did not touch is still caught by --full.
Changing one byte and committing invalidates every reused result for that branch.
No assertion is removed or weakened.
verification: Reviewer re-measures on its own runs, breaks one test in an untouched suite to confirm --full catches it, and tries to obtain a reused PASS for a commit that never passed.
tasks.baseline: Night run of 5 October 2026: 120 verify minutes in 398; 11 of 25 passing runs repeated suites that had already passed on the same commit (37 minutes); check about 106 s per run; the auth suite ran 18 times.
lenses: security: the reuse record is the thing being trusted; try to get a false PASS out of it

tasks.title: Verify speed 2: stop verification growing with every wave
deliverables: Inner loop: while fixing, the cook runs only the suites and test files the change touches (seconds, not minutes). The full named suites run once on the final commit.

One full local run per wave: the cook's inner loop is scoped, and the pass runs the full named suites once on the final commit (a recorded PASS on that exact commit is reused). The off-machine run stays a safety net on master that nobody waits for.

Hillclimb test:box-package: find where its two minutes go (clean-directory installs, repeated exports, typechecks) and remove repeats, for example one exported Box and one install shared by tests that only read it.

Ratchet: kitchen-stats holds a budget for the executed seconds of one full verify and fails loudly when a wave pushes it over. The head chef lowers it after each gain. A wave that needs to raise it says so in its brief.
acceptance: Counts as well as seconds, before and after, on the same commit: installs performed, exports performed, suites executed, full local runs per wave.
A test written first proves a real break in the shared packaging setup is still caught; no assertion is removed or weakened.
The budget check fails on a fabricated run that exceeds it.
verification: Reviewer re-measures, and breaks the exporter on a scratch branch to confirm the suite still fails.
tasks.condition: Met on R1: verification was 22.5 of 46 minutes. Runs when the owner names it.
tasks.baseline: Executed, passing runs: test:box-package went from 21-51 s to 117-131 s between 5 Oct 18:00 and 6 Oct 00:15 as waves added tests; check went from about 65 s to about 100 s in a day. R1 spent 22.5 of 46 minutes in verification across five executed runs of about 4.5 minutes.

tasks.title: Verify speed 3 (superseded by K7a): parallel tests, leak fixes, budgets and attribution in one wave
deliverables: Stop the leaks first, because they grow with every run: each packaging test removes the temp folders it creates when it finishes, pass or fail; the time-budget recorder removes its own files; and verify, when it starts, stops and clears any embedded database a killed earlier run left behind (its own data folders only). On 6 October 2026 one afternoon left 5,805 test folders, 206 recorder files and an orphaned database that had run for over two hours.

Run the packaging suite's test files in parallel, three workers to start (six cores, 16 GB), leaving every other suite as it is. Each test file already makes its own temp folders; find and fix anything files share (caches, fixed folder names, ports) before turning parallelism on, with a test written first that shows the collision.
Then take the two slowest test files and remove repeated setup inside them, only where the numbers show it.
The time budget applies to whichever verify profile a wave actually ran, per profile, and reads the latest run that has a summary. A killed run is reported as killed, not as a missing budget.
Lower the budget to the new measured time plus a small margin, and record before and after: seconds and peak memory for one full run, as the median of five executed runs on the same commit.
Any test that only passed because it ran alone is fixed or reported by name. Going back to one worker without saying so is not an option.
acceptance: Five consecutive executed full runs pass on the same commit with parallel workers; a single flaky failure in those five means the wave is not done.
No assertion is removed or weakened, and the same number of tests run as before.
A deliberately broken packaging test still fails the run.
Peak memory during the suite stays under what the machine can give with the kitchen's agents running; record the figure.

After a full run the system temp folder holds no box-d21-*, box-k6-* or kitchen-verify-pg* items and no database process is left; after a run that is killed part-way, the next run clears what it left.
verification: Reviewer checks the test count is unchanged, breaks one packaging test on a scratch branch to see the run fail, and reads the five-run record; it does not need to repeat all five.
tasks.condition: Run only if the numbers after K6 still show verification above 15% of a run.
tasks.unpaused: By the CTO on 6 October 2026: verification was 32 of 70 minutes on A1 and 38 of 71 on A2, so it now blocks milestone A in practice. The owner raised the same concern.
tasks.baseline: Executed, passing runs on 6 October 2026: the packaging suite took 172 to 235 s (it was 25 to 34 s on 5 October), check about 86 s, build about 18 s; a full run is about 5 to 6.5 minutes. The suite runs its 19 test files one at a time (maxWorkers 1). Slowest files: verify.test.ts 55 s, command-checks.test.ts 43 s, submission.test.ts 23 s. The time budget from K6 reported MISSING because the latest run of its one named profile had no summary, and A2 used a different profile, so the ratchet saw nothing.
lenses: measurement fairness: before and after on the same commit, five runs each, with spread
tasks.daytimeOnly: Edits scripts/verify.mjs, which is read-only overnight. Parked at kickoff on the night of 6 October 2026 for that reason and because the night's one-run limit ruled out its measurement.
tasks.measurementAllowance: Up to ten executed full verify runs in this wave: five on the base commit and five on the final commit, back to back, no waiting between them. This is the one exception to "one executed full run per candidate".
tasks.result: Parked 7 October 2026 with an independent FAIL. It bundled six separate jobs and a ten-run measurement into one wave: 500 changed lines in 14 files, 12 full runs against 10 allowed, no clean final run. The CTO wrote it too large. Its branch wave/K7 is kept as a source to salvage from. Replaced by K7a; the rest returns to the backlog as separate small items.

tasks.title: Run the full verify off this machine on every push
tasks.ownerApproval: 6 October 2026: the owner approved using GitHub Actions on the private repository (free tier, no paid minutes).
deliverables: A GitHub Actions workflow on the private repository runs a frozen install and node scripts/verify.mjs --full on a Linux runner and uploads the run logs. It runs on pushes to master that change code, tests, scripts or dependencies; pushes that touch only documents, kitchen files, briefs or agent profiles do not trigger it.
The install policy gains the Linux entry embedded-postgres needs. No secrets, no deploys, no other triggers, no paid runners.

The head chef reads the latest run result with the gh command line at every kickoff and after every merge to master, including overnight. A red run on master comes first: no new wave starts until a fix wave has made it green, and STATUS.md says so while it is red. START.md and KITCHEN.md gain one line each for this, written by the head chef when the wave closes.

Stay inside the free allowance (2,000 Linux minutes and 500 MB a month for a private repository): a newer push cancels a run still in progress, logs are kept for three days, and the job has a ten-minute timeout. If runs approach the allowance, switch to one run per wave merge plus one nightly run, and say so in STATUS.md.
acceptance: A push with a deliberately broken test on a scratch branch (workflow temporarily pointed at it) fails the run; master passes.
The workflow uses only the free tier and no secret is configured.
A document-only push starts no run; a second push while a run is in progress cancels the first.
The wave file records the minutes one run actually used.
With a deliberately red run on a scratch branch standing in for master, a kickoff reports it and declines to start the next wave.
verification: Reviewer reads the workflow for triggers, permissions and secrets, and checks one real run's log against a local verify on the same commit.

tasks.title: Run the delegation loop on a public repository that is not ours
tasks.proposal: Agreed as the step after R2 (owner, 6 October 2026). Starts when the owner names it in a START message.
deliverables: Choose a well-known public TypeScript project and one real open issue with a clear expected behaviour, preferably one with a failing test or a reproduction. Pin the exact commit. Record why this project and this issue, and which candidates were rejected and why.

A readiness report for that repository, before any issue is chosen: how much of it is ready to hand work out as it stands. Which of its tests travel into a Box and still run, which do not and why, which of a sample of its open issues could be prepared as a Box today and what blocks the others. This is what an owner would need to see first, and it is produced by reading and running their code locally only.

Prepare the Box with the product as it is after R2, writing no code for this request. Time the preparation and record every manual step. Anything the product could not do is a named preparation gap, not something to patch around quietly.
A blind recipient solves it from the Box alone. Owner-side verify runs against a clean clone of that project at the pinned commit.

Record: preparation minutes and steps, files and bytes disclosed against the project total, what the recipient lacked, each check and its result on the untouched code, and whether the result was accepted.
Report against the "useful" milestone in PLAN.md, one line per condition: met, not met, or not tested.
acceptance: No code specific to this request or this project is added under packages/. General fixes the run exposes are allowed and listed.
Nothing is sent to the other project: no issue, comment, pull request or message. Their code is only read and run locally.
Their code is third-party code: dependencies are installed with install scripts disabled, and its build and tests run inside a container, never directly on the host.
A failed run is a valid result. The report says which condition of the milestone failed and why.
verification: Reviewer repeats the export from the pinned commit, reruns owner-side verify, checks nothing left the machine, and recounts the disclosure figures.
lenses: security: third-party code handling and nothing sent outward
measurement fairness: preparation time and manual steps are complete

tasks.title: Prototype the neutral core before building it
tasks.result: Done 6 October 2026, PASS as a prototype. The neutral loop worked on npm, Python and multi-package fixtures with no outside dependencies. Findings are in waves/A0.md and research/box-delegation/a0/RESULT.md and are carried into A1, A2 and A4.

tasks.title: A neutral agreement format
tasks.ownerApproval: 6 October 2026: milestone A approved; the first wave still waits for "go" on its pre-cook card.
deliverables: An agreement declares setup commands and check commands as a program plus arguments, for any program, each with its working directory, role (guard or outcome), who runs it (owner or recipient) and a timeout. No enumerated list of tools.
An agreement describes the environment the solver needs in plain terms (programs and versions the owner states), as information for the solver. The core does not require or interpret tool versions.

Every existing agreement, fixture and test moves to the new format in this wave, and the old format, its tool list and the pnpm-specific handling of declared commands are deleted. One format, not two.

Behaviour that must not change: checks are run on the untouched code at export and recorded; a do-nothing submission is rejected; edits outside the editable paths are rejected; the product makes no sandbox claim for declared commands.

One rule for starting a declared program, with no shell: the program is a real executable found on the search path, or an interpreter plus a script path that travels with the Box. On Windows a command-file shim (such as npm) may be started through the system command interpreter only when every argument is free of that interpreter's special characters; otherwise it is refused with a message saying how to declare it. The rule is tested as a property.
Before running anything, export and verify check that every declared program can be found and name any that cannot, so a missing tool is a named gap and never a failed check.

Declared paths and working directories are contained on canonical paths, and nothing the product deletes is outside a folder it created in that run. The A0 prototype did neither and is not to be copied.
acceptance: No file under packages/box-package names pnpm, TypeScript or a test runner in the agreement schema or in how declared commands are run.
Every existing Box test passes after migration with no assertion weakened; tests of the deleted pnpm verb handling are removed with it and listed.
node scripts/verify.mjs --full test:box-package test:kitchen exits 0 inside the budget.
verification: Reviewer greps the schema and command runner for tool names, re-runs R2's delegation through the migrated agreement, and confirms the base-check and no-op evidence is unchanged.
lenses: security: declared commands still spawn from an argument array with no shell, inside the checked directory

tasks.title: Neutral file selection
deliverables: The default way to choose a Box's files is an owner-declared list (paths and patterns), checked for exclusions and containment on canonical paths exactly as today.

Export proves the list by execution: setup and guard checks run in a clean folder outside the repository that holds only the Box. A missing file shows up as a failing guard on the untouched code and is reported as a named gap.
Following TypeScript imports moves out of the core into an optional helper that proposes a file list for the owner to accept. The core works with the helper absent.
The project's own dependency manifest and lockfile travel unchanged. The core does not rebuild a lockfile.
A clean setup is never evidence: A0 showed a locked install exits 0 with a needed sibling package missing. Only checks prove a Box.

An outcome check must fail for the right reason: export runs it in the owner's full repository as well as in the Box on the untouched code, and requires the same result in both. A check that fails in the Box but passes, or fails differently, in the full repository is reported as an incomplete Box.
The report to the owner says what the unchanged dependency files disclose, including the names of packages that were left out.
acceptance: With the TypeScript helper removed from the run, export still produces a working Box from a declared list.
A declared list that omits a needed file is caught at export, by name.
The excluded-path protections from D2.1 hold: case-aliased and junctioned paths cannot ship excluded files.
verification: Reviewer exports with and without the helper, removes one needed file from a list to see the gap named, and replays the D2.1 exclusion attacks.
lenses: security: exclusion and containment on canonical paths

tasks.title: Export and verify with no built-in package manager
deliverables: Export and owner-side verify run the agreement's declared setup commands instead of a hard-coded install. Nothing in the core spawns pnpm by name.
Generated TypeScript scaffolding (package manifest, compiler configuration, generated evaluators) leaves the core. What a Box needs to build is what the owner's files and setup commands provide.
The submission tool and owner-side verification work from file contents and hashes only, for files of any type.
acceptance: A repository-wide search of the core for pnpm, tsc, vitest, tsconfig and package.json finds none outside the optional helper and tests.
R1's and R2's delegations still pass end to end through the neutral path.
node scripts/verify.mjs --full test:box-package test:kitchen exits 0 inside the budget.
verification: Reviewer runs the search, re-runs R2 end to end, and confirms a do-nothing submission is still rejected.

tasks.title: Proof on two projects unlike ours
deliverables: Two small committed fixture projects written for this purpose: one JavaScript project managed by npm, and one Python project with no JavaScript in it. Each has a guard test and a request with a check that fails on the untouched code.

The whole loop on each with no code written for either project: export, checks on the untouched code, a blind recipient working from the folder alone, owner-side verify, a do-nothing submission rejected.
A short report: what the owner had to declare for each, how long preparation took, and anything the core still assumed.

A third fixture: a multi-package project with real outside dependencies, to show how a cut-down slice installs when the dependency file lists outside packages for members that were left out. This needs a small download, done with install scripts disabled, of a well-known package with no install scripts of its own.
acceptance: Both loops complete with zero lines added under packages/ for either project.
Dependency setup for the fixtures runs with install scripts disabled where the tool supports it, and the fixtures have no third-party install scripts.
Anything the core still assumed is listed as a gap, not patched around.
verification: Reviewer repeats both exports and owner-side verifies, and reads the diff for anything project-specific.
lenses: measurement fairness: preparation time and manual steps are complete

tasks.title: Replay recently fixed issues on a public repository
tasks.result: Done 7 October 2026 in two waves, both PASS WITH NOTES. R3b-1 screened tj/commander.js: 8 bug-fix candidates, 3 replayable cases with a linked issue. R3b-2 took one (issue #2614) through the product: owner-side verify accepted a blind solver's one-line change and rejected a no-op; the pass rebuilt the case independently and matched. Export needed six attempts: the paired check refuses any test runner that prints run times, and exported only with that output silenced. Replay, one case, one solver; solver saw the acceptance test and was blind by instruction only. Useful milestone still unmet.

tasks.title: Run the packaging tests on three workers, and nothing else
tasks.daytimeOnly: Only if scripts/verify.mjs has to change; the aim is that it does not.
tasks.why: A full verify run is about six and a half minutes (median 393 s over five clean runs on 7 October 2026) and each wave needs several. The packaging suite is most of that and runs its test files one at a time on a six-core machine.
deliverables: The packaging suite runs its test files on three workers. Every other suite stays as it is.

Only the collisions that parallel running actually exposes are fixed, each with a test that shows it. Take what is already proven from the parked wave/K7 branch (its three-worker scoped run passed 146 tests) and leave the rest there.
Nothing else: no leak fixes, no stale-database recovery, no budget or statistics changes, no slow-file tuning, no memory sampling. Those are separate backlog items.
acceptance: Two executed full runs on the final commit both pass: node scripts/verify.mjs --full --fresh test:box-package test:kitchen. That is the whole measurement; the before figure is the 393 s already on record.
The same number of tests run as before, with no assertion removed or weakened, and a deliberately broken packaging test still fails the run.
If the full run is not at least a minute faster, say so and do not merge: the change is not worth its risk.
The existing time budget is left where it is. Lowering it is a later, separate step.
verification: Reviewer checks the test count, breaks one packaging test on a scratch branch to see the run fail, and relies on the two recorded runs.

tasks.title: Report, do not judge
Fewer things to supply
tasks.proposal: create records one line of why (required, short, kept in the record and shown to a later agent); title taken from the task when not given; a sensible default place to write; evidence gathered by the tool for the note (the failing output, files changed so far against the base); box bounty help shows the whole journey on one screen; every success line ends with the exact next command; close the known rough edges (status outside a checkout names the right verb; status repeats conflict paths if BT3a left any gap). The agent still writes the task itself: a badly worded task wastes the bounty.

tasks.title: Tell the agent: the skill, the description, the owner's limits
tasks.proposal: Three separate, switchable pieces: (1) the tool description: what it does, when it is worth using, when it is not, in a few lines, with full instructions loaded only on use; (2) lines for a project's agent rules, including an "open bounties" line the tool keeps current so a later agent sees it where it already looks; (3) reminders at moments of difficulty, stated as facts, off by default. Plus the owner's limits file (what may leave, what may be spent, whether a clean mechanical pass may be applied without asking), which also gives the agent the facts it needs to choose: cost, limits, expected wait or "not yet known", how the answer will be judged. Nothing enforces use. Accepted by the constructed scenarios in PLAN.md ("How BT4 is accepted"): better-choice and not-better situations, every alternative listed and accounted for, a few steps not a whole job, scored on reasoning, each scenario attacked by the pass before use. Two or three wordings tried; the best kept.

tasks.title: The kitchen uses it: one real bounty, end to end
tasks.proposal: Three parts, kept apart. (1) The journey: a person asks for a bounty on this repository's own work; a blind solver started outside every checkout answers; a different session collects it from the record alone. Proves it works; says nothing about demand. (2) Judgement: one or two of BT4's scenarios run in full, climbing from description only, to the rules note, to a reminder, to a person asking, stopping at the first rung where the agent chooses sensibly; then the easy control at that rung. Record what it did instead when it did not post: kept trying, reported failure, or claimed success. (3) Open: the tool stays installed during ordinary waves, nobody mentions it, and the recorded reasons are read afterwards. Report all three honestly, including "nobody used it". One real use before many; capped budgets.

tasks.title: The first bounty posted outside
tasks.ownerApproval: Required separately, with the choice of site. Sending anything outside is the owner's decision and never happens overnight.
tasks.proposal: An adapter to one existing bounty site, after an hour's reading of how those sites accept a task posted by a program, how they verify and how they pay. Once money moves, accepting cannot be undone the way a merge can: design a window before payment is final and how disputes are handled before this wave is briefed.
